info.name: Smart Money — Adaptive Engine (Insights + Suggestions)
info.description:
User-driven end-to-end flow for the redesign adaptive engine: trait onboarding → seed trailing history → trigger insights → receive yes/no suggestions → accept/dismiss → verify side effects.

FIXED PAST-MONTH SCENARIO (demo-friendly, date-independent): everything is dated in a fixed window — baseline in Feb/Mar/Apr 2026, trigger on 15 May 2026 (mid-month, day 15, past the MIN_PACE_DAYS guard). Because the SuggestionProducer analyzes `asOf = the transaction's own date`, this fires identically no matter what the real calendar date is — so you can demo/test early in the real month.

GET /insights normally analyzes `LocalDate.now()`, so it wouldn't see May data today. The insight requests therefore pass `?asOf={{asOfInsights}}` (=2026-05-15) to analyze the seeded month deterministically. This param is a testing/demo aid.

SEE docs/api-testing/README.md for prerequisites (a PRE-VERIFIED account, and the recommended `app.suggestion.daily-cap=0` / `cooldown-hours=0` test profile so the fatigue layer doesn't hide the functional path).

exec: // FIXED past-month scenario — deterministic regardless of the real date (see collection desc).
// Baseline: Feb/Mar/Apr 2026. Trigger: 15 May 2026 (mid-month, past MIN_PACE_DAYS).

request.description: Uses a PRE-VERIFIED account (registration needs multipart + an email OTP via /auth/verify-email; not automatable here). Captures the bearer token used by every later request.

interventionLevel GENTLE is REQUIRED for pushed suggestions (NOTIFY / null = pull-only, no suggestions ever). GENTLE means the push gate = WARN. savingPace BALANCED scales CONTRIBUTE amounts to 20% of disposable. focusMode REDUCE_SPENDING orders GET /insights spending-first.

item.name: 1 — Seed trailing baseline (3 months)
item.description: Backdated via the transaction `date` field (dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm). Amounts are chosen so the baseline itself stays quiet (no suggestion fires while seeding): FOOD is flat (stddev 0 → no anomaly), and each month has too little trailing history to trigger anything. This gives the analyzer the >=3 months it needs before the trigger month.

item.name: 2 — RAISE_BUDGET flow
item.description: Category HAS a budget → an over-pace expense trips BUDGET_PACE → producer raises a RAISE_BUDGET suggestion. Accept → the budget's limit is raised to the resolved value.

Trigger: FOOD expense on May 15 (2,000,000) — over pace

request.description: By day 15 of 31, 2,000,000 spent projects to ~4,130,000 — past the 3,000,000 limit (ratio ~1.38 → CRITICAL) → BUDGET_PACE. The producer runs synchronously inside this create. The proposed raise is income-capped (20,000,000 income, so no cap binds here).
The accepted RAISE_BUDGET executed Create/UpdateBudget with amountLimit = resolvedValue (> 10,000,000). Verify the FOOD limit moved. Adjust the field path below if the list DTO differs.

item.name: 3 — CREATE_BUDGET flow
item.description: Category has NO budget → a spike trips OVERSPEND_ANOMALY → producer raises CREATE_BUDGET (resolvedValue = trailing-3-month median). Accept → a new budget is created for the trigger month.

request.description: Baseline ENTERTAINMENT ~1,000,000 with real variance → a 5,000,000 month is a large z-score → OVERSPEND_ANOMALY. No ENTERTAINMENT budget exists → producer picks the CREATE_BUDGET path.

exec: pm.test('payload has month+year+resolvedValue', () => { const a = s.payload.proposedAction; pm.expect(a.month).to.exist; pm.expect(a.year).to.exist; pm.expect(a.resolvedValue).to.exist; });

item.name: 4 — CONTRIBUTE_TO_PROJECT flow
item.description: An INCOME event with savings headroom (SAVINGS_CAPACITY) toward an active saving project → producer raises CONTRIBUTE_TO_PROJECT (amount = disposable × pace, capped at remaining). Accept → a real contribution is recorded on the project.

request.description: Must be an ACTIVE, non-group saving project with room to receive. priority may be optional; remove it if your ProjectPriority enum differs.
Getting paid is the moment the producer checks savings headroom (maybeProduceSavingsContribution). disposable = avgIncome (~20,000,000) - recurring (0) - committed budgets.

exec: pm.test('payload has projectId+resolvedValue', () => { const a = s.payload.proposedAction; pm.expect(a.projectId).to.exist; pm.expect(Number(a.resolvedValue)).to.be.above(0); });

item.name: 5 — Idempotency & dismissal
item.description: Responding twice must NOT re-run the action; dismissing is the negative path.

request.description: Second response returns the current (already-decided) state without executing the action again — the RespondToSuggestionUseCase flips PENDING->decided conditionally.

exec: pm.test('at least one suggestion deep-link', () => pm.expect(deep.length, 'expected app://suggestions/{id} links').to.be.above(0));

item.name: 7 — SET_CATEGORY_LIMIT flow
item.description: A budgetless category trending UP (CATEGORY_TREND) but NOT a monthly anomaly → producer raises SET_CATEGORY_LIMIT (resolvedValue = trailing-3-month median). Accept → a first budget is created for the trigger month. TRANSPORTATION climbs 1.0M → 1.5M → 3.0M → 3.2M: the 4-month slope is a clear upward trend, but the trigger month's z-score stays below WARN so OVERSPEND_ANOMALY does NOT steal the branch (CREATE_BUDGET only wins when the anomaly qualifies).

request.description: Trailing [1.0M,1.5M,3.0M] mean ~1.83M, stddev ~0.85M → trigger 3.2M is z~1.6 (< 2 → below WARN, no anomaly), while the 4-point slope is strongly positive → CATEGORY_TREND. No TRANSPORTATION budget exists → producer falls through CREATE_BUDGET to SET_CATEGORY_LIMIT.

exec: pm.test('payload: TRANSPORTATION + month/year + resolvedValue, no budgetId', () => { const a = s.payload.proposedAction; pm.expect(a.category).to.eql('TRANSPORTATION'); pm.expect(Number(a.month)).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('triggerMonth'))); pm.expect(Number(a.year)).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('triggerYear'))); pm.expect(Number(a.resolvedValue)).to.be.above(0); pm.expect(a.budgetId == null, 'budgetId should be null for a create').to.be.true; });

item.name: 8 — REDUCE_BUDGET flow
item.description: A budgeted category consistently used well under its limit (BUDGET_UNDERSPEND) → producer raises REDUCE_BUDGET (resolvedValue = median actual + 15% headroom). Accept → the budget limit is lowered. CLOTHING history is a flat ~1.0M/mo against a 5.0M limit; the trigger is a small 0.5M expense so the current-month pace also stays well under the limit (both the historical median and the projection must sit <= 60% of the limit).

item.name: Create CLOTHING budget (limit 5,000,000) for trigger month
Trigger: CLOTHING on trigger day (500,000) — well under pace

request.description: 500,000 by mid-month projects to ~1.0M, far under the 5.0M limit (<= 60% threshold). Trailing median 1.0M is likewise under → BUDGET_UNDERSPEND. No BUDGET_PACE fires (projection under limit), so the producer's reduce branch runs.

exec: pm.test('payload: budgetId + resolvedValue below current limit', () => { const a = s.payload.proposedAction; pm.expect(a.budgetId).to.exist; pm.expect(Number(a.resolvedValue)).to.be.above(0); pm.expect(Number(a.resolvedValue)).to.be.below(5000000); });

The ping arrives as a notification with deepLink app://transactions; its content is the raw i18n key (notification.insight.large_transaction|SHOPPING) when server narration is off.

item.name: 12 — REVIEW_SUBSCRIPTION flow (Wave 2, acknowledge-only)
item.description: A stable recurring charge (EDUCATION 'online course' at 500,000 for 3 months) posts at 700,000 (+40%, past the ±15% tolerance band) → SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_HIKE (WARN) → REVIEW_SUBSCRIPTION suggestion on the expense-create path. Acknowledge-only: the payload has NO proposedAction, and accepting executes nothing — Yes just marks the hike reviewed. EDUCATION must have no budget and the series is chosen so neither OVERSPEND_ANOMALY (flat baseline, stddev 0) nor CATEGORY_TREND (growth < 10%/mo) steals the branch.

Different amount from the seeds → no DUPLICATE_CHARGE; stddev 0 per-charge history → no LARGE_TRANSACTION.

item.name: 13 — Monthly recap: CASHFLOW_NEGATIVE + INCOME_DROP (Wave 3, notification-only)
item.description: The month-rollover recap judges the month that just CLOSED — facts no transaction event can trigger (a vanished income is a transaction that never happened). Normally MonthlyRecapScheduler runs this on the 1st; here the property-gated demo endpoint (app.demo-triggers.enabled=true REQUIRED) runs the same use case with an explicit asOf. NO new seeds needed — folders 0–12 already built the story: July has 20M income but ~24M+ of expenses (cashflow negative), and August has NO income against a flat 20M/month baseline (critical income drop). Run after folders 0–12.

item.name: 15 — INCREASE_CONTRIBUTION: project off track (Wave 4)
item.description: A saving project falling behind has NO transaction to react to — the problem is the contributions that DIDN'T happen — so ProjectHealthScheduler judges pace weekly; here the demo endpoint (app.demo-triggers.enabled=true REQUIRED) runs the identical pass with an explicit asOf. Unlike folders 0–14 this scenario uses DYNAMIC dates: a project's createdAt is the real clock (the API sets it), so the pace judgment must be anchored to the real 'today'. The math is still fully deterministic: target 12,000,000, deadline = the 15th three months from now, 1,000,000 contributed this month, judged on the 1st of next month → 3 saving months left, remaining 11,000,000 → required 3,666,666.67/mo vs observed 1,000,000/mo → ≥2× shortfall → CRITICAL → INCREASE_CONTRIBUTION ask. Accepting contributes the catch-up amount — which crosses 25% progress and sets up folder 16's milestone ping.

request.description: Dynamic dates (see folder description): deadline pinned to the 15th of month+3 so monthsLeft is always exactly 3 when judged from the 1st of next month.

item.name: 19 — REALLOCATE_BUDGET flow (UC1)
item.description:
A budgeted category on pace to overshoot (BUDGET_PACE), where ANOTHER budget the same month is confirmed underspent (BUDGET_UNDERSPEND) with enough headroom → the producer offers REALLOCATE_BUDGET INSTEAD of RAISE_BUDGET: a zero-sum snapshot that raises the overflowing budget and lowers the underused one by the same amount (committed total unchanged, so it never trips BUDGET_OVER_INCOME). Accept applies the whole snapshot atomically.

Uses the collection's fixed demo window: baseline in the three seed months (Apr/May/Jun 2026), trigger on 15 July 2026 — same convention as folders 2/3/7/8. FOOD is the overflowing recipient (3M limit, a 2M mid-month expense projects over it); ENTERTAINMENT is the underspent donor (5M limit, flat ~1M history + a tiny early-month expense). The donor's headroom (~4M) fully covers FOOD's gap (~1.1M), so reallocation is preferred over a raise. Because FOOD and ENTERTAINMENT are the same categories folders 2–3 budget in July, run this folder on a FRESH account (folder 0 first), not in the same pass as folders 2–3.

item.name: Create FOOD budget (limit 3,000,000) for the trigger month

request.description: The category that will overflow — the reallocation RECIPIENT.

item.name: Create ENTERTAINMENT budget (limit 5,000,000) for the trigger month

request.description: A roomy limit against a flat ~1M/month history — the underspent DONOR. FOOD (3M) + ENTERTAINMENT (5M) = 8M committed, well under the 20M income, so no BUDGET_OVER_INCOME / REBALANCE fires.

item.name: Seed donor ENTERTAINMENT expense (500,000) early in the trigger month (day 2) — no premature ask

request.description: Dated day 2 (< MIN_PACE_DAYS = 3) so the producer's pace/underspend detectors bail on THIS create — no REDUCE_BUDGET is raised for ENTERTAINMENT yet. By the day-15 trigger the donor's spent is 500,000 (projects to ~1M, well under its 5M limit → BUDGET_UNDERSPEND), leaving ~4M of headroom to donate.

item.name: Trigger: FOOD overshoot on the trigger day (2,000,000)

request.description: 2,000,000 by day 15 of 31 projects to ~4,130,000 — past the 3,000,000 FOOD limit → BUDGET_PACE. The producer runs synchronously: the budgeted branch tries REALLOCATE first, finds ENTERTAINMENT can fully cover the ~1.1M gap, and raises REALLOCATE_BUDGET instead of RAISE_BUDGET.

exec: pm.test('BUDGET_UNDERSPEND(ENTERTAINMENT) present (a valid donor)', () => pm.expect(us, JSON.stringify(items)).to.exist);
const s = items.find(x => x.type === 'REALLOCATE_BUDGET' && typeof x.dedupKey === 'string' && x.dedupKey.indexOf('REALLOCATE_BUDGET:FOOD:2026-07') === 0);
pm.test('REALLOCATE_BUDGET(FOOD) pending exists', () => pm.expect(s, JSON.stringify(items.map(x => x.dedupKey))).to.exist);

pm.test('preferred over a raise: no RAISE_BUDGET(FOOD) for the same month', () => pm.expect(items.find(x => x.type === 'RAISE_BUDGET' && String(x.dedupKey).indexOf('RAISE_BUDGET:FOOD:2026-07') === 0)).to.not.exist);
pm.test('donor never cut below its own spend (>= 0, stays positive)', () => pm.expect(Number(ent.newLimit)).to.be.above(0));
pm.test('zero-sum: the deltas cancel out', () => { const net = adj.reduce((sum, x) => sum + (Number(x.newLimit) - Number(x.currentLimit)), 0); pm.expect(Math.abs(net)).to.be.below(1); });

request.description: Applies the consented snapshot to BOTH budgets atomically (same executor as REBALANCE_BUDGETS). If a donor had spent past its lowered limit by now, the whole ask would be rejected (nothing changes) — the born-exceeded guard.

item.name: GET /budgets — assert FOOD up, ENTERTAINMENT down, total unchanged

exec: const food = Array.isArray(items) ? items.find(b => b.category === 'FOOD') : null;
const ent = Array.isArray(items) ? items.find(b => b.category === 'ENTERTAINMENT') : null;
pm.test('FOOD limit raised above its original 3,000,000', () => pm.expect(Number(food.amountLimit)).to.be.above(3000000));
pm.test('ENTERTAINMENT limit lowered below its original 5,000,000', () => pm.expect(Number(ent.amountLimit)).to.be.below(5000000));
pm.test('committed total unchanged (~8,000,000 — zero-sum move)', () => pm.expect(Math.abs(Number(food.amountLimit) + Number(ent.amountLimit) - 8000000)).to.be.below(1));
